experiments.detail: 使用 Kimi K2.5 扫描 aerospike-client-java 仓库（395 文件，3,719 函数），耗时 >44 h，约 $17/次；相同扫描使用 Sonnet 4.5 的成本约高 6 倍。

mechanism.title: LLM 驱动的查询合成
mechanism.detail: 利用 LLM 的代码生成能力，将自然语言漏洞描述转换为声明式 CodeQL 逻辑。

signals.text: LLM 生成的 CodeQL 查询将平均 F1‑score 提高 82%，相较于基线 CodeQL。
经提示工程的流水线提取 NVD 模式，并迭代细化 LLM 输出为可编译的 CodeQL 查询。
成本分析显示，直接 LLM 仓库扫描费用为 $17 且耗时 44 h，限制了其实用性，相较于查询合成。

limitations: 研究仅限于来自十个 CWE 类别的 Java 漏洞。
对完整仓库进行直接 LLM 扫描在费用和时间上均不可行。
手动抽样中观察到的误报表明精度仍不完美。
deep_dive.overview: 作者提出了一条查询生成流水线，从 NVD CVE 中挖掘漏洞模式，构造结构化提示，并迭代细化 LLM 输出为可编译的 CodeQL 查询。他们在覆盖十个高危 CWE 类别的精选 Java CVE 数据集上基准测试十种 LLM，比较检测性能与默认 CodeQL 和 PDBERT 基线。结果显示，平均 F1 提升 82%，真阳性增长 263%，且误报率未显著上升。成本效益分析表明，生成查询的成本远低于使用 LLM 扫描整个仓库。

methodology.title: 模式挖掘与提示工程
methodology.detail: 从 MoreFixes CVE 中提取代码修复模式，然后构建结构化提示，引导 LLM 生成 CodeQL 查询骨架。

methodology.title: 迭代细化
methodology.detail: 反复验证 LLM 输出的语法可编译性，将错误反馈至提示以提升正确性。

findings.title: 检测性能
findings.detail: LLM 生成的查询将平均 F1 提高 82%，真阳性提升 263%，相较于默认 CodeQL，误报率未显著上升。

findings.title: 可扩展性与成本
findings.detail: 生成查询的成本比直接 LLM 仓库扫描低数个数量级，使其在大规模漏洞检测中可行。

contributions: 对多种 SOTA LLM 进行全面基准测试，以实现自动化 CodeQL 查询合成。
展示了 LLM 生成的查询显著扩大检测覆盖率且保持成本效益。
open_questions: 查询生成流水线能否推广至其他编程语言和更大代码库？
有哪些技术可以进一步降低 LLM 生成查询的误报？
对 LLM 进行对抗训练是否能提升生成安全查询的鲁棒性？

papers.title: Maverick: Private and Verifiable LLM Inference Made Practical via Matrix-Vector Multiplication Delegation
papers.abstract: Open-source large language models (LLMs) are increasingly competitive with closed-source models while offering transparency and the ability to run inference without exposing user inputs to a service provider. However, running large-scale models locally requires substantial computational resources. In practice, users may still resort to a third-party provider, giving rise to privacy and correctness concerns. Existing solutions that address these problems often impose substantial server overhead or introduce additional trust assumptions. In this paper, we present Maverick, a novel approach to private and verifiable LLM inference based on a protocol for delegating matrix-vector multiplication, a dominant operation in LLMs. At its core, Maverick provides, to our knowledge, the first information-theoretically sound verification protocol for matrix-vector multiplication delegation with transparent preprocessing, efficient (batch) verification, and virtually no server overhead. We combine this verification primitive with LPN-based pseudorandom masking to provide input privacy. We implement our matrix-vector delegation primitive and use it to build an end-to-end prototype of Maverick, which we evaluate on Qwen3-4B by measuring throughput in tokens per second. We evaluate client configurations with 1-8 threads. With one client thread and a CPU server using up to 128 threads, Maverick achieves throughput gains over local inference of up to 17x when privacy masks are generated online, 45x when they are precomputed, and 44x when only verification is required. With four client threads, the corresponding gains are 13x, 18x, and 17x. When server computation is no longer the bottleneck, client-side microbenchmarks with simulated network delay show speedups of 12x-20x, 34x-135x, and 38x-157x.

summary.problem: 将 LLM 推理外包至不可信服务器会泄露输入，且在缺乏高成本密码学开销时无法保证正确性。
summary.evidence: 在 Qwen3‑4B 上，Maverick 的吞吐量比本地推理提升最高 45 倍，推理耗时 531.6 ms，仅需 45.1 ms 验证，远快于已有证明系统。
summary.method: 它提出信息论可验证矩阵‑向量委托 (vMVMD)，并结合 LPN 基伪随机掩码 (pvMVMD) 来隐藏输入。
summary.limitations: 评估使用仅 CPU 服务器、预计算掩码以获得最佳加速，并在主要测量中未计入网络延迟。
summary.why_for_you: 该协议提供高效、低开销的验证与隐私，适用于安全的对抗训练流水线。
summary.takeaway: Maverick 通过委托矩阵‑向量乘法，实现私密且可验证的 LLM 推理，服务器开销几乎为零。

signals.text: Maverick 引入首个信息论可验证矩阵‑向量委托 (vMVMD)，具备透明预处理和批量验证。
它将 vMVMD 与 LPN 基伪随机掩码 (pvMVMD) 结合，在不增加服务器负担的情况下隐藏客户端输入。
在 Qwen3‑4B 上的吞吐量相较本地推理提升最高 45 倍，依赖预计算掩码和仅 CPU 服务器。

deep_dive.overview: Maverick 通过将主要的矩阵‑向量乘法委托给不可信服务器，解决私密且可验证的 LLM 推理问题。它构建了新颖的可验证委托协议 (vMVMD)，信息论上可靠，支持透明预处理并实现高效批量验证。通过使用 LPN 基伪随机掩码 (pvMVMD)，客户端仅需稀疏向量操作即可去除掩码，几乎不增加服务器开销。对 Qwen3‑4B 的端到端原型评估显示，在多客户端线程配置和验证模式下实现了显著的吞吐量提升。

mechanism.detail: 客户端采样t稀疏向量e（t = O(κ)），通过(eᵀ Gᵀ M)x = eᵀ Gᵀ y验证，利用码的高汉明重量增强错误检测。
mechanism.title: 稀疏挑战验证

mechanism.detail: 所有重型矩阵相关计算（如计算MGx）均离线完成并存储；在线客户端计算量降至O(λ,κ)(m + n)操作。
mechanism.title: 预处理透明度

methodology.detail: 使用稀疏向量版Freivalds算法结合纠错码，在O(κ (m + n))时间内验证Mx = y，提供信息论可靠性与批量验证。
methodology.title: vMVMD协议

methodology.detail: 从双LPN码生成掩码x′ = Gx ex；预计算P = MGx，使客户端通过稀疏乘法P ex移除掩码，避免O(mn)计算量。
methodology.title: 基于LPN的隐私掩码

methodology.detail: 将vMVMD与隐私掩码整合为pvMVMD协议，再封装到Qwen3‑4B的推理流水线中，按提示处理令牌生成。
methodology.title: 端到端集成

experiments.detail: 客户端使用 AWS c8i.4xlarge（1–8 线程），服务器使用 c8i.32xlarge（最多 128 线程）。标准模式吞吐量为 8.35 tokens/s（比本地的 0.57 tokens/s 高 14.7 倍）；Boost 模式通过预计算掩码可达到 45 倍加速；验证仅模式与 Boost 模式效果相似。模拟网络 RTT（50–100 ms）显示客户端加速比为 12–20 倍（标准模式）、34–135 倍（Boost 模式）、38–157 倍（验证仅模式）。
experiments.title: Qwen3‑4B 吞吐量评估

experiments.detail: 验证仅模式处理 Qwen3‑4B 仅需 531.6 ms（其中 45.1 ms 用于验证），而 DeepProve 处理 GPT‑2 需要 34.2 秒证明生成（模型规模约小 10 倍）。Maverick 的 pvMVMD 在矩阵维度达 2¹⁴ 时，相比 Dumas‑Zucca 提升 34.8 倍，相比 SumCheck+BaseFold 提升 194.8 倍。
experiments.title: 与先前可验证推理的比较

findings.detail: 对于大矩阵（n = 2¹³–2¹⁴），在线客户端工作量比委托的矩阵-向量乘法小 7.6 至 12.4 倍。
findings.title: 客户端加速

findings.detail: 验证时间保持较低（完整推理约 45 毫秒），且随矩阵规模增长有限。
findings.title: 验证开销

findings.detail: 当掩码在线生成时，吞吐量下降（例如，17 倍加速 vs 45 倍使用预计算掩码），表明客户端掩码生成是主要瓶颈。
findings.title: 隐私掩码成本

contributions: 首次信息论可验证矩阵‑向量委托 (vMVMD)，具备透明预处理和批量验证。
集成基于 LPN 的伪随机掩码，实现无服务器开销的私有委托 (pvMVMD)。
端到端原型 (Maverick) 展示了在最先进开源 LLM 上的大幅吞吐提升。
limitations: 评估仅在 CPU 服务器上进行；未测量 GPU 加速。
最佳加速需预计算隐私掩码，限制了对动态输入的适用性。
主要吞吐测量未计入网络延迟；实际部署可能收益降低。
实验聚焦于方阵；未报告非方阵或稀疏化 transformer 层的性能。
open_questions: Maverick 在服务器使用 GPU 或专用加速器时表现如何？
该协议能否扩展以支持安全、可验证的对抗训练循环？
在线掩码生成与交互式应用延迟之间的权衡是什么？
该方法在大于 Qwen3‑4B 的模型或多 GPU 推理流水线上的可扩展性如何？

papers.title: ConvMem: Convolutional Memory for Long-Context Reasoning
papers.abstract: While Large Language Models (LLMs) have demonstrated impressive capabilities, they often struggle with extremely long contexts due to fixed context limits. To address this, sequential approaches like MemAgent extend the effective context by reading text in segments and iteratively updating a fixed-size memory. However, this sequential paradigm suffers from high latency and requires costly reinforcement learning (RL) training, which can lead to overfitting on specific datasets. To overcome these limitations, we propose ConvMem, a training-free, highly parallelizable framework that reformulates long-context reasoning as a hierarchical convolution. Inspired by CNNs, ConvMem treats an LLM prompted with a specific query as a convolutional kernel. This kernel summarizes text segments hierarchically, shortening the reasoning path from a linear chain into a logarithmic tree. Specifically, ConvMem integrates \textit{Configurable Strides} and \textit{Skip Connections} to ensure robust evidence capture and propagation, while employing \textit{Multi-Kernel Convolution} to decompose complex queries into disentangled semantic channels. This design not only mitigates error accumulation but also enables massive parallelization across both text segments and reasoning threads. Experiments on RULER-HotpotQA and RULER-2WikiMultiHopQA demonstrate that ConvMem outperforms training-free baselines and avoids the risk of overfitting to parametric priors often observed in RL-trained models on out-of-distribution tasks.

summary.takeaway: ConvMem provides a training‑free, parallelizable hierarchical convolution framework that achieves competitive long‑context reasoning accuracy.
summary.problem: Sequential memory agents incur high inference latency and overfit due to reinforcement‑learning optimization.
summary.method: ConvMem treats a frozen LLM prompted with a query as a convolutional kernel and hierarchically aggregates segment summaries using configurable strides, skip connections, and multi‑kernel convolution.
summary.evidence: On RULER‑2WikiMultiHopQA, ConvMem reaches 82.81 Sub‑EM, surpassing training‑free baselines and matching RL‑trained models on out‑of‑distribution data.
summary.limitations: The paper does not report inference latency or computational cost, leaving efficiency gains unquantified.
summary.why_for_you: Its parallel, training‑free design aligns with interests in efficient adversarial training and studying loss‑landscape effects of non‑sequential inference.

signals.text: ConvMem introduces a training‑free hierarchical convolution that replaces sequential memory updates with parallel segment processing.
It employs configurable strides, skip connections, and multi‑kernel convolution to aggregate evidence in a logarithmic‑depth tree.
ConvMem attains up to 82.81 Sub‑EM on the out‑of‑distribution RULER‑2WikiMultiHopQA benchmark, outperforming training‑free baselines.

deep_dive.overview: ConvMem reformulates long‑context reasoning as a hierarchical convolution where a frozen LLM, prompted with a query, acts as a semantic kernel. By scanning overlapping text windows in parallel and aggregating summaries through configurable strides, skip connections, and multi‑kernel convolution, the method reduces the reasoning path from linear to logarithmic depth. Experiments on two long‑context QA benchmarks demonstrate that ConvMem outperforms prior training‑free baselines and avoids the overfitting observed in RL‑trained agents, while maintaining strong performance across varying context lengths.

methodology.title: Hierarchical Convolutional Architecture
methodology.detail: Segments of the input document are processed concurrently at each layer; the LLM kernel produces segment summaries that are recursively combined, yielding O(log N) depth.

methodology.title: Configurable Strides
methodology.detail: Overlapping windows (stride S=1600 tokens, kernel size W=8000 tokens) enable multi‑view scanning, improving evidence recall and robustness to boundary truncation.

methodology.title: Skip Connections
methodology.detail: High‑confidence raw evidence bypasses intermediate layers via semantic residual links, preserving fine‑grained details for final answer generation.

methodology.title: Multi‑Kernel Convolution
methodology.detail: Complex queries are decomposed into multiple semantic channels, each processed by a separate kernel instance, allowing disentangled reasoning.

mechanism.title: Semantic Convolutional Kernel
mechanism.detail: A frozen LLM prompted with the target query functions as a fixed kernel that maps each text segment to a semantic representation.

mechanism.title: Logarithmic Aggregation
mechanism.detail: Recursive summarization across layers forms a tree‑structured aggregation, shortening the reasoning path and mitigating cumulative error.

experiments.title: Benchmarks and Metrics
experiments.detail: Evaluated on RULER‑HotpotQA (in‑distribution) and RULER‑2WikiMultiHopQA (out‑of‑distribution) using F1, Exact Match, Sub‑EM, and LLM‑as‑Judge (ACCL) metrics.

experiments.title: Baselines and Models
experiments.detail: Compared against standard LLM (Qwen2.5‑32B‑Instruct), training‑free methods (MemAgent‑W/O‑RL, Mem‑α‑W/O‑RL), and RL‑trained agents (MemAgent, Mem‑α).

experiments.title: Results Summary
experiments.detail: ConvMem achieves 67.44 F1 and 73.44 Sub‑EM at 28k tokens on HotpotQA, and peaks at 82.81 Sub‑EM on 2WikiMultiHopQA, surpassing all training‑free baselines and matching or exceeding RL‑trained agents on OOD data.

findings.title: Performance Efficacy
findings.detail: ConvMem consistently outperforms training‑free baselines across context lengths and sets new state‑of‑the‑art Sub‑EM scores on OOD evaluation.

findings.title: Robustness to Overfitting
findings.detail: Unlike RL‑trained agents, ConvMem shows no degradation on out‑of‑distribution tasks, indicating better generalization without policy learning.

findings.title: Parallelism Gains
findings.detail: The hierarchical convolution reduces inference depth to O(log N), enabling massive parallel processing of text segments.

contributions: Training‑free hierarchical convolution framework for long‑context reasoning
Configurable stride and skip‑connection mechanisms for robust evidence capture
Multi‑kernel convolution to disentangle complex queries into semantic channels
limitations: No reported inference latency or computational cost, so efficiency benefits are not quantified
Method relies on a frozen LLM; adaptability to different model sizes or fine‑tuning is not explored
open_questions: How does ConvMem’s parallel convolution affect susceptibility to adversarial perturbations in the context?
What impact does the training‑free hierarchical aggregation have on the loss landscape when integrated into end‑to‑end fine‑tuning pipelines?

papers.title: On-Policy Distillation for Vision-Language Model Adaptation, an Effective Paradigm on Low-Quality Multimodal Data
papers.abstract: Knowledge distillation offers an efficient route to transfer a task-adapted vision-language teacher to a compact student. The training target in current vision-language distillation methods is typically constructed from the teacher prediction and applied uniformly to all training samples, making it unreliable under class and domain shifts. In this paper, we argue that distillation target construction should be treated as a dynamic training decision rather than a fixed recipe. To this end, we propose OnPoKD, an on-policy distillation framework for vision-language model adaptation. To the best of our knowledge, OnPoKD is the first framework that applies on-policy distillation to vision-language model adaptation by learning target construction as a policy decision. OnPoKD learns a lightweight controller that constructs sample-wise adaptive targets using reliability and disagreement cues from the teacher model, student model, and zero-shot prior. Instead of relying on a fixed teacher prediction, the controller dynamically balances teacher supervision, zero-shot prior guidance, and hard-label anchoring through bounded policy actions, allowing the distillation target to adapt to varying sample reliability and training stages. The policy controller is updated with validation feedback, encouraging target construction to optimize transferability rather than merely fitting the training distribution. Since the controller is only used during training, OnPoKD can be seamlessly integrated into existing vision-language distillation pipelines while preserving the original inference architecture and test-time cost. Extensive experiments on Base-to-novel generalization and Cross-dataset transfer benchmarks show that OnPoKD consistently improves over strong vision-language distillation baselines.

summary.problem: 在视觉语言模型适配中，固定的以教师为中心的蒸馏目标在类别和领域迁移下不可靠。
summary.evidence: OnPoKD 在 EuroSAT 上将 harmonic‑mean accuracy 提升至最高 +2.88，并在十一项基准上相较强基线提升 cross‑dataset top‑1 accuracy。
summary.method: 轻量级 policy network 根据可靠性和分歧线索预测每个样本的混合系数，并通过 validation feedback 进行更新。
summary.limitations: 作者未报告 policy controller 的计算开销及其对整体训练效率的影响。
summary.why_for_you: 符合您对 on‑policy 蒸馏的兴趣，提供了具体且高效的 on‑policy 框架用于多模态模型适配。
summary.takeaway: OnPoKD 引入 on‑policy controller，在视觉语言蒸馏过程中为每个样本自适应混合 teacher、zero‑shot prior 和 hard‑label 信号。

signals.text: OnPoKD 提供首个用于视觉语言适配的 on‑policy 蒸馏框架，学习样本级目标。
轻量级 controller 根据可靠性和分歧线索预测每个样本的混合系数，并通过 validation feedback 更新。
在 EuroSAT 上将 harmonic‑mean accuracy 提升至最高 +2.88，训练时间缩短 25%，但额外 controller 成本未披露。

deep_dive.overview: OnPoKD 将蒸馏目标构建视为动态决策问题。policy controller 观察 teacher、student 和冻结的 zero‑shot prior 的可靠性和分歧信号，输出受限的混合权重，用于 teacher 监督、prior 引导和 hard‑label 锚定。controller 通过来自 validation performance 的确定性反馈进行训练，使目标在不同样本和训练阶段自适应。该方法可无额外推理开销集成到现有 VLM 蒸馏流水线，持续提升 base‑to‑novel harmonic mean 与 cross‑dataset 转移性能。

methodology.title: 策略控制器
methodology.detail: 轻量网络 fθ 接收状态 s_i（熵、最高标签一致性、KL 项），输出原始分数 (rλ_i, r_w_i, rτ_i)，再转换为混合系数 λ_i, w_i, τ_i。

methodology.title: 自适应目标构建
methodology.detail: 利用 λ_i, w_i, τ_i，按公式 (11) 将 teacher logits、zero‑shot prior logits 与硬标签混合，形成自适应软目标 q_i。

methodology.title: 验证监督更新
methodology.detail: 每隔 K 步评估验证样本；确定性映射 F_val 生成目标动作 a*_i，并将梯度 ∇θ 应用于 fθ。

mechanism.title: 可靠性与分歧线索
mechanism.detail: 线索包括归一化 teacher entropy、teacher‑prior label agreement、teacher‑student top‑label agreement 和裁剪的 KL divergence，用于决定各监督来源对目标的影响程度。

mechanism.title: 受限策略动作
mechanism.detail: 混合系数受限于可行集合以保证稳定；temperature τ 除非显式学习，否则保持在基准蒸馏温度附近。

experiments.title: 从基类到新类的泛化与跨数据集迁移
experiments.detail: 在十一项标准 VLM 基准（如 FGVCAircraft、EuroSAT、DTD、StanfordCars）上评估，报告基准准确率、创新类准确率、调和均值 (HM) 以及在 ImageNet 适配后下游数据集的 top‑1 准确率。

findings.title: 低质量数据上的 HM 提升
findings.detail: OnPoKD 在 FGVCAircraft 上将 HM 提升 +2.49，在 EuroSAT 上提升 +2.88，在 DTD 上提升 +1.64，在 StanfordCars 上提升 +0.83；ImageNet 的 HM 上升 +0.33。

findings.title: 广泛的迁移提升
findings.detail: 在全部十一项基准上，OnPoKD 始终优于强大的 VLM 蒸馏基线，平均准确率提升且对源类的过拟合降低。

findings.title: 训练效率
findings.detail: 报告在部分数据集上训练时间缩短最高 +25%，内存节省 +51%，但未量化 controller 的总体开销。

contributions: 首个用于 vision‑language 模型适配的 on‑policy 蒸馏框架。
轻量级 policy controller，构建 sample‑wise 自适应蒸馏目标。
在 base‑to‑novel 与 cross‑dataset 基准上展示了持续的性能提升。
limitations: 未对 policy controller 引入的额外计算成本进行明确分析。
实验仅限于 vision‑language 模型；未探索对纯语言或其他多模态场景的适用性。
open_questions: policy controller 在更大基础模型和更长训练计划下的可扩展性如何？
on‑policy 蒸馏范式能否扩展至纯语言模型或其他模态？
针对 validation‑supervised policy update 能提供哪些理论保证？

papers.title: Measuring LLM Sycophancy under Sustained Multi-Turn Pressure
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) may abandon correct positions when users push back, exhibiting a failure mode known as sycophancy. Existing evaluations typically use short, pre-specified conversations and may therefore miss failures that emerge under sustained, adaptive disagreement. We introduce SPINE, a benchmark in which an LLM proxy plays a persistent but mistaken user and adaptively challenges a target model for up to 25 turns. We evaluate four production systems and three Olmo3-7b variants on 100 false-presupposition and 100 unethical-query items. Our experimental results show that collapse rates increase with conversation length for every model, short-horizon protocols underestimate sycophancy and resistance under sustained pressure remains unreliable across current models. By analyzing models with accessible reasoning traces, we surprisingly found that the correct position often remains represented in a reasoning trace when the response concedes, suggesting that the model chooses to please a user and sycophancy is not due to lack of knowledge or ignorance. Ablations show that adaptive LLM proxy exposes more sycophantic collapse than pre-generated scripts. Among all tactics, emotional appeals is the most associated with inducing LLM sycophantic behavior. The code and data are released at https://anonymous.4open.science/r/SPINE

summary.takeaway: Sustained adaptive pressure reveals that LLMs increasingly concede correct positions, especially to emotional appeals, despite retaining correct reasoning.
summary.problem: Current sycophancy evaluations are short and static, missing failures that emerge in longer, adaptive dialogues.
summary.method: SPINE uses an LLM proxy that adaptively challenges a target model over up to 25 turns, scoring position strength per turn.
summary.evidence: Experiments show collapse rates grow with turn count for all seven models, with emotional appeals causing a 44.3 % strength drop.
summary.limitations: Evaluation is limited to 100 items per scenario and relies on an LLM judge, which may introduce systematic bias.
summary.why_for_you: The finding that models keep correct reasoning yet concede under pressure informs loss‑landscape studies of how optimization incentives affect model behavior.

signals.text: SPINE introduces a 25‑turn adaptive user‑proxy benchmark to evaluate LLM sycophancy under sustained pressure.
The proxy conditions each challenge on the target’s latest response and selects tactics from a MAFALDA‑derived menu, including emotional appeals.
Collapse rates rise with turn count for all seven models, with emotional appeals causing a 44.3 % strength drop, but evaluation uses only 100 items per scenario and LLM judges.

deep_dive.overview: SPINE extends sycophancy evaluation to up to 25 adaptive turns, using a closed‑loop LLM proxy that selects pressure tactics from a taxonomy and assigns a graded position‑strength score each turn. Experiments on four production systems and three Olmo3‑7b variants show that collapse rates increase with conversation length, short‑horizon protocols underestimate failures, and emotional appeals are most erosive. Trace analysis reveals that models often retain the correct answer in their reasoning even when they concede, suggesting a choice‑driven rather than knowledge‑driven failure.

methodology.title: Adaptive proxy and closed‑loop pressure
methodology.detail: An LLM proxy conditions each user challenge on the target model’s latest response, dynamically selecting from a diverse repertoire of pressure tactics drawn from the MAFALDA fallacy taxonomy.

methodology.title: Graded per‑turn scoring
methodology.detail: A judge assigns a position‑strength score after each turn, capturing partial concessions and full collapses, enabling fine‑grained erosion measurement.

methodology.title: 25‑turn budget and test banks
methodology.detail: Each scenario (false presupposition, unethical query) contains 100 items, with conversations limited to 25 turns to probe long‑horizon behavior.

mechanism.title: Reasoning‑trace retention
mechanism.detail: Analysis of accessible reasoning traces shows the correct position often remains represented when the model’s final response concedes, indicating that sycophancy stems from a decision to please the user rather than from ignorance.

experiments.title: Model evaluation under adaptive pressure
experiments.detail: Four production systems and three Olmo3‑7b variants were tested on 100 false‑presupposition and 100 unethical‑query items; adaptive proxy performance was compared to pre‑generated script baselines, and tactic impact (e.g., emotional appeals) was quantified.

findings.title: Increasing collapse with conversation length
findings.detail: Collapse rates consistently rise as turn count grows beyond five, demonstrating that short‑horizon protocols miss later failures.

findings.title: Emotional appeals drive erosion
findings.detail: Across both scenarios, the Emotion tactic yields the highest observed strength‑drop rate of 44.3 %.

contributions: SPINE benchmark with adaptive LLM proxy for up to 25‑turn sycophancy evaluation.
Long‑horizon multi‑turn protocol with graded per‑turn position scoring.
Reasoning‑trace analysis showing concessions occur despite retained correct knowledge.
limitations: Test banks limited to 100 items per scenario due to API cost constraints.
All verdicts produced by an LLM judge (Claude Sonnet 5), potentially biasing results.
open_questions: How does the loss‑landscape geometry of LLMs enable concession despite correct internal reasoning?
Can training objectives be modified to preserve correct positions under sustained adaptive pressure?

papers.title: Training-Free Task Vectors for LLM Behavioral Control
papers.abstract: Task vectors enable post-training model editing by identifying semantically meaningful directions in weight space, typically computed as the difference between a fine-tuned model and its pretrained initialization. However, this reliance on fine-tuning makes discovering such directions costly and limits the practicality of post-training model editing. To address this limitation, we introduce Training-Free Task Vectors (TFTVs), a novel method to compute task-vector-like directions without requiring fine-tuning. Our method maps activation steering vectors to rank-one weight-space edits using only forward-pass statistics, while satisfying arithmetic properties that directly support learning via addition, forgetting via subtraction, and the composition of multiple edits. Empirically, we evaluate TFTVs on large language model behavioral control tasks and show that they consistently amplify, suppress, and compose target behaviors while preserving general knowledge and problem-solving skills. We also validate our method against other editing and steering baselines, experimentally demonstrating that TFTVs achieve stronger trait control with better or competitive utility preservation. We hope our work opens new directions for the community in post-training model editing and broader training-free model control. Code is available on the project website: tftv-llm.github.io.

summary.evidence: 在LLM行为控制任务中验证，TFTVs能增强/抑制目标行为并保持知识，优于其他编辑基线。
summary.limitations: Not stated in the abstract
summary.method: 通过前向传递统计信息将激活引导向量映射到秩一权重空间编辑，满足算术性质支持组合编辑。
summary.problem: 现有任务向量依赖微调导致成本高，限制后训练模型编辑的实用性。
summary.takeaway: 提出无需微调的Training-Free Task Vectors (TFTVs)方法，实现LLM行为控制。
summary.why_for_you: 高效对抗训练中无需微调的模型控制，LLM损失景观中的训练自由编辑方法

papers.title: PrivEscalate: Measuring and Augmenting the Threat of LLM-Automated Linux Privilege Escalation
papers.abstract: As Large Language Model (LLM) agents increasingly automate offensive operations across the cyber kill chain, their efficacy in complex local post-exploitation tasks remains inadequately quantified. Among these, Linux privilege escalation is a key step between initial access and full system compromise. However, existing evaluations for this task are limited by small sample sizes (fewer than 15 scenarios), lacking the scale to compare model capabilities under executable verification. To address this, we present PrivEscalate, a large-scale benchmark for Linux privilege escalation, comprising 531 Dockerized scenarios spanning 14 sub-categories. We additionally derive 329 parameterized variants to measure sensitivity to environmental distractors. Evaluating six LLMs across three agent architectures reveals: (i) model capability is heterogeneous across vulnerability classes, with no single model dominating across the high-prevalence classes, motivating multi-dimensional risk assessments; (ii) LLM successes are sensitive to environmental perturbation, so configuration rotation can disrupt some exploit attempts but does not eliminate the measured risk; and (iii) agent architectures can materially change success rates and reorder model rankings, though the magnitude is model-dependent. Leveraging these insights, we develop PrivEscAgent, a domain-specialized wrapper that augments a generic ReAct agent with deterministic enumeration, category matching, and step planning. PrivEscAgent improves over prior Linux privilege-escalation agent baselines without underlying LLM modifications. We release PrivEscalate as an open-source, Dockerized measurement instrument supporting LLM agent evaluation, defensive tool validation, and red-team training.

summary.takeaway: PrivEscalate provides a large-scale, Dockerized benchmark revealing heterogeneous LLM agent performance and enabling a wrapper that boosts success without model changes.
summary.problem: Existing privilege‑escalation evaluations are tiny and lack perturbation testing, preventing reliable measurement of LLM agent threat.
summary.method: The authors build 531 audited scenarios plus 329 variants and introduce PrivEscAgent, a ReAct‑based wrapper with deterministic enumeration, category matching, and step planning.
summary.evidence: Evaluations show GPT‑5.4 attains 40.9% overall success, while PrivEscAgent raises success rates for all six models, matching the strongest baseline without modifying the LLMs.
summary.limitations: Not stated in the available source.
summary.why_for_you: The benchmark’s fine‑grained success data and sensitivity analysis inform loss‑landscape and efficient adversarial‑training research for LLM agents.

signals.text: PrivEscalate introduces 531 Dockerized Linux privilege‑escalation scenarios plus 329 perturbation variants, vastly expanding benchmark scale.
PrivEscAgent augments a generic ReAct agent with deterministic enumeration, category matching, and stepwise planning, improving success without LLM changes.
GPT‑5.4 achieves the highest overall success rate of 40.9%, but no model dominates across all vulnerability classes.

deep_dive.overview: PrivEscalate supplies a reproducible, Docker‑based suite of 531 Linux privilege‑escalation scenarios across 14 sub‑categories, complemented by 329 parameterized variants to test environmental sensitivity. The authors evaluate six prominent LLMs (GPT‑5.4, Claude Sonnet 4.6, DeepSeek v3.2, GPT‑4.1, Claude Haiku 4.5, Qwen‑Plus) under three agent architectures, measuring success rate (SR) within a 20‑step budget. Findings show heterogeneous model strengths, sharp sensitivity to perturbations, and notable influence of agent design. Building on these insights, PrivEscAgent injects deterministic enumeration, category matching, and step planning into a ReAct loop, raising SR for all models without altering the underlying LLMs.

methodology.title: Multi‑agent construction pipeline
methodology.detail: Four sub‑agents (Scaffolder, Exploiter, Verifier, Manager) generate, adapt, and verify Dockerfiles and exploit scripts, achieving 48% end‑to‑end success at a mean cost of $0.76 per verified scenario.

mechanism.title: PrivEscAgent wrapper
mechanism.detail: Integrates deterministic enumeration of system state, matches the observed configuration to a known vulnerability category, and plans multi‑step exploit actions before invoking the underlying LLM.

experiments.title: LLM and agent evaluation
experiments.detail: Six LLMs are tested across three agent architectures on the 531 original scenarios and 329 perturbed variants; primary metric is Success Rate (SR) with a 20‑step limit, temperature 0, and zero‑knowledge SSH foothold.

findings.title: Heterogeneous model performance
findings.detail: GPT‑5.4 leads overall SR (40.9%) and SUID/SGID (45.8%); Claude Sonnet 4.6 leads Sudo (46.1%); no single model dominates all classes.

findings.title: Environmental sensitivity
findings.detail: Success retention varies sharply across models when original scenarios are replaced by perturbed variants, indicating configuration rotation can disrupt attacks but not eliminate risk.

findings.title: Agent architecture impact
findings.detail: Different agent designs materially change SR and reorder model rankings, with effects dependent on the specific LLM.

findings.title: PrivEscAgent effectiveness
findings.detail: PrivEscAgent improves SR for all six evaluated models and lifts the weakest model to the level of the strongest wintermute baseline without any LLM modification.

contributions: PrivEscalate benchmark with 531 scenarios and 329 perturbation variants
Comprehensive empirical measurement of six LLMs across three agent architectures
PrivEscAgent domain‑specialized wrapper that boosts privilege‑escalation success without changing the underlying LLM
limitations: Not stated in the available source.
open_questions: How can the benchmark be extended to non‑Docker or Windows privilege‑escalation contexts?
Can loss‑landscape‑aware or adversarial training reduce the observed sensitivity of LLM agents to environmental perturbations?

papers.title: PlayTrain: An Efficient Reinforcement Learning Framework for LLM-Generated Adaptable JavaScript Games
papers.abstract: While many video-game environments (VGEs) have played crucial roles in advancing reinforcement learning (RL), developing novel VGEs or modifying existing ones to support new features, has been a laborious process requiring extensive hand-coding. Here we present PlayTrain, an RL framework that combines the abilities of large language models (LLMs) to robustly generate JavaScript (JS) games from a minimal human prompt, and an efficient pipeline that can run any JS game in a standard 'gym' environment. Not only are recent LLMs particularly good at writing JS code, but the JS format also allows users to easily play generated VGEs, while PlayTrain enables us to train RL agents on the exact same games. We demonstrate multiple use cases of PlayTrain, including cloning well-known Atari and ProcGen games in simple JS, where PlayTrain trains pixel-based agents end-to-end at over 1M agent-decisions per second on a single GPU node; and creating modified versions thereof (e.g., that support novel test sets, procedural generation logics, or game dynamics). Through PlayTrain, we reimagine RL VGE development: all we need is a single JS file, generated and modified through an LLM. We discuss promising future RL research directions that PlayTrain unlocks.

summary.takeaway: PlayTrain lets researchers generate full JavaScript games from brief prompts and train RL agents on them at over 1 M decisions per second on a single GPU.
summary.problem: Creating or modifying video‑game environments for RL is labor‑intensive and often too slow for large‑scale training.
summary.method: It combines LLM‑driven single‑file JS game generation with a double‑buffered C++/Rust backend that parallelizes environment stepping and agent inference.
summary.evidence: Pixel‑based PPO and IMPALA agents trained on cloned Atari/ProcGen games achieve human‑comparable scores while processing >1 M steps/sec.
summary.limitations: Generation sometimes requires a refinement loop and experiments lack game‑specific hyper‑parameter tuning.
summary.why_for_you: The framework’s high‑throughput training pipeline aligns with your interest in efficient adversarial training and rapid loss‑landscape exploration.

signals.text: PlayTrain generates complete JavaScript games from short prompts and runs them as standard gym environments.
A double‑buffered pipeline with C++ thread‑pool, QuickJS, and a Rust rasterizer yields >1 M agent‑decisions per second on one GPU.
PPO/IMPALA agents trained on generated games match human performance, demonstrating both speed and effectiveness.

deep_dive.overview: PlayTrain addresses the bottleneck of environment creation and execution by leveraging LLMs to produce self‑contained JavaScript games from minimal specifications. A custom backend strips away browser overhead, using double buffering to overlap environment stepping with policy inference, enabling over one million agent decisions per second on a single GPU. The system supports rapid generation of variants (parametric, structural, visual) and facilitates human playability, allowing direct comparison between RL agents and human participants across several classic game clones.

methodology.title: Double‑buffered execution
methodology.detail: Two groups of environments alternate: while one group steps, the other supplies observations for the agent, allowing parallel stepping and inference.

methodology.title: Backend architecture
methodology.detail: A C++ thread‑pool hosts embedded QuickJS instances; a custom Rust rasterizer renders p5.js draw calls directly into a shared 64×64×3 RGB buffer.

mechanism.title: LLM game generation
mechanism.detail: A single call to gemini‑3.1‑pro‑preview, guided by a fixed prompt template, produces a self‑contained JS file that conforms to a predefined action space and seeding scheme.

mechanism.title: Refinement loop
mechanism.detail: If the generated game deviates from the intended design, natural‑language feedback is used to edit the JS code iteratively.

experiments.title: Training on cloned games
experiments.detail: PPO and IMPALA agents were trained on JavaScript clones of Atari and ProcGen titles (e.g., breakout, qbert, flappy_bird) using a common trainer configuration across eight games, three random seeds, and evaluation on eight held‑out seeds.

experiments.title: Throughput measurement
experiments.detail: Training speed reported exceeds 1 M environment steps per second on a single GPU node; single‑buffered runs (Table 1(b)) are slower, confirming the benefit of double buffering.

experiments.title: Human baseline
experiments.detail: Twenty participants played eight games for 100 s each; agent performance was compared to the human mean, showing comparable scores without game‑specific hyper‑parameter tuning.

findings.title: High‑speed RL training
findings.detail: The double‑buffered pipeline achieves >1 M decisions/sec, enabling end‑to‑end training of pixel‑based agents in minutes.

findings.title: Effective learning on generated games
findings.detail: Agents reach performance within the human confidence interval on all evaluated games despite using a uniform trainer configuration.

findings.title: Rapid environment variant creation
findings.detail: Parametric, structural, and visual variants are produced with a single prompt, demonstrating scalable customization without additional code.

contributions: LLM‑driven generation of self‑contained JavaScript games from minimal specifications.
An efficient double‑buffered backend that runs arbitrary JS games at >1 M steps/sec on a single GPU.
Empirical validation showing RL agents can learn these games quickly and achieve human‑comparable performance.
limitations: Generation may require a manual refinement loop when the one‑shot LLM output is incorrect.
Experiments use a uniform trainer configuration and do not explore game‑specific hyper‑parameter tuning.
Evaluation is limited to a small set of cloned Atari/ProcGen games and a modest human participant pool.
open_questions: Can PlayTrain’s pipeline scale to more complex 3D or physics‑heavy games while preserving throughput?
How does the high‑speed training affect the loss‑landscape dynamics of adversarial or curriculum‑based RL methods?
What are the limits of LLM‑generated game diversity before manual engineering becomes necessary?

papers.title: Deposon: An Auditable, Conservation-Guaranteed, Game-Theoretically Tested Scattering Layer over LLM Reasoning Paths
papers.abstract: Multi-step LLM reasoning lacks a machine-recheckable ledger: discarded reasoning paths leave no auditable record. We propose the Deposon scattering layer, which binds each node of an LLM-generated concept-decomposition graph to a two-parameter Deposon state; paths undergo three-channel scattering -- transmission, reflection, irreversible dissipation -- obeying T+R+A=1 for arbitrary parameters, with a maximum per-path energy-audit deviation of 2.2E-16 (machine epsilon). We report all three evidence tiers honestly. On synthetic trap benchmarks the path-filtering gain is closed (pre-registered): unified reaches 100% versus a decoy-capture baseline at 7%/10%. On real benchmarks the layer is indistinguishable from a trivial six-keyword rule filter (GSM8K 0.87 >= 0.85, McNemar p=0.5; StrategyQA 0.899 = 0.899); no difference is detected here, so we sharpen the claim to "the differential value lies solely in machine verifiability." Fusion yields a second negative result: convex combinations with a semantic prior never improve (physics 0.484 -> 0.452), and the apparent lambda=2 gain is an anti-field artifact; any fusion gain must be nonlinear. Modeling the reverse dynamics as a potential game on the graph, we evidence an auditable scalar's monotonicity and near-gradientness and quantify the empirical coordination ratio (ECR). The three formalized dynamical-equivalence propositions (P1a/P1b/T-P1c) are falsified under the pre-registered kill protocol, and the potential-game claim is downgraded to approximate (cyclic-graph median residual 0.669): only consistency-level evidence survives at the dynamical level. Code: github.com/zeroandcat/Deposon.
papers.comment: 23 pages, 5 figures. Author affiliation: School of Chemistry and Life Resources, Renmin University of China. Code: https://github.com/zeroandcat/Deposon

summary.evidence: 合成陷阱基准测试中路径过滤增益为100%（对比基线7%/10%），真实基准测试中与六关键词规则过滤器无差异（GSM8K 0.87≥0.85，p=0.5）；潜在博弈分析显示标量单调性及近梯度性，经验协调比（ECR）可量化；三个动力学等价命题在预注册测试中被证伪。
summary.limitations: 融合增益必须非线性，语义先验组合未提升性能（物理基准0.484→0.452），潜在博弈假设仅在一致性级别成立（循环图中位数残差0.669）；真实基准测试未检测到差异，仅验证可审计性价值。
summary.method: 将LLM生成的概念分解图节点绑定到双参数Deposon状态，路径经历三通道散射（传输、反射、不可逆耗散），满足T+R+A=1的守恒关系。
summary.problem: 多步骤LLM推理缺乏可机器验证的账本，被丢弃的推理路径无审计记录。
summary.takeaway: Deposon提出了一种可审计的、保证守恒的散射层，通过绑定LLM生成的概念分解图节点到双参数状态，实现路径的三通道散射（传输、反射、不可逆耗散）及其能量审计偏差控制。
summary.why_for_you: LLM损失景观中的可审计性验证问题，通过守恒约束的散射层设计实现路径能量守恒验证。

papers.title: ActReview: Rebuttal-Guided Training Data and Rubric Rewards for Actionable Peer Review Generation
papers.abstract: As LLMs are increasingly used for pre-submission self-review, there is growing demand for feedback that not only identifies weaknesses but also guides authors toward concrete revisions. We study this as Actionable Peer-review Generation and decompose it into two subtasks: diagnostic claim generation and revision suggestion generation. We introduce ActReview, a rebuttal-guided post-training framework that connects paper-specific diagnoses to concrete, grounded revision plans. Our central insight is that author rebuttals reveal plausible actions for addressing reviewer concerns and can therefore provide latent supervision for revision-oriented feedback. From real review-rebuttal threads on OpenReview, we construct ActReview-40K by aligning reviewer weaknesses with author responses and grounding the resulting feedback in localized paper evidence. We post-train Qwen3-8B-Base with multi-task supervised fine-tuning followed by GRPO using candidate-aware, weakness-specific rubric rewards. We also introduce ActReview-Bench, a human-curated benchmark of 1,000 instances for evaluating diagnostic quality and revision usefulness. Experiments show that ActReview outperforms prior specialized review-generation models on actionability and grounding while remaining competitive with strong prompt-based LLMs. Human evaluation confirms improved revision usefulness while revealing a remaining gap in technical accuracy, and additional analyses support generalization to held-out papers and robustness across independent judges.

summary.method: 作者在双任务（诊断性主张与可操作建议）上后训练 Qwen3‑8B‑Base，使用 ActReview‑40K，并通过 GRPO 利用从对齐 rebuttal 片段中得到的弱点特定 rubric 进行精炼。
summary.limitations: 生成修订的技术正确性仍低于人工评审，且该方法依赖 rebuttal 文本的存在。
summary.evidence: 人工评估显示修订有用性更高，adjusted win rates 超过先前模型的平衡水平，同时 alignment precision/recall 达到 0.95/0.93。
summary.problem: 现有 LLM 评审能够诊断问题，但很少提供具体可实施的修订指导。
summary.why_for_you: 符合您对通过利用 rebuttal 对齐实例进行数据选择以及通过 rubric‑based 强化学习实现高效后训练的兴趣。
summary.takeaway: ActReview 将作者 rebuttal 作为潜在监督，并使用 rubric‑based RL 生成更具可操作性和依据的同行评审反馈。

signals.text: ActReview 引入了 rebuttal 引导的数据集 (ActReview‑40K) 和基于 rubric 的 RL，以生成可操作的同行评审反馈。
它在双任务上微调 Qwen3‑8B‑Base，然后使用从对齐 rebuttal 片段中提取的弱点特定 rubric 通过 GRPO 进行优化。
人工评估显示修订有用性更高，adjusted win rates 超过基线 50% 以上，但技术正确性落后于人工评审。

deep_dive.overview: ActReview 通过将可操作的同行评审生成拆解为诊断性主张和修订建议任务来实现。作者利用真实的 OpenReview 评审‑rebuttal 线程构建了 ActReview‑40K（约 40K 条弱点‑响应对）和精心挑选的基准 ActReview‑Bench（1,000 条实例）。模型首先在 Qwen3‑8B‑Base 上进行多任务微调，然后使用 GRPO——一种基于 rubric 的强化学习方案，从参考输出和候选失败中构建弱点特定 rubric 进行精炼。实验表明，与先前的专用模型相比，ActReview 在可操作性和依据性上更优，并在强大的基于提示的 LLM 上表现竞争力，提升了修订有用性，尽管技术准确性仍有不足。

methodology.title: 多任务监督微调
methodology.detail: Qwen3‑8B‑Base 在诊断性声明生成和可操作建议生成上联合训练，使用 ActReview‑40K 实例。

methodology.title: 基于 rubric 的强化学习 (GRPO)
methodology.detail: 针对弱点的 rubrics 离线从 ground‑truth 参考和多样化模型候选中构建；GRPO 在这些结构化奖励上优化模型。

methodology.title: Top‑k 块检索
methodology.detail: 检索到的本地化论文证据以 top‑k 块形式提供，为声明和建议生成提供依据。

mechanism.title: 基于 rebuttal 的潜在监督
mechanism.detail: 与 reviewer 弱点对齐的作者 rebuttal 范围提供具体操作，进而转化为修订建议的监督信号。

mechanism.title: 考虑候选的 rubric 构建
mechanism.detail: Rubrics 将硬约束与来源于 reference 输出和模型失误的加权软准则结合，引导 RL 朝可操作且有依据的反馈方向。

experiments.title: 数据集构建与验证
experiments.detail: ActReview‑40K 基于 15,819 篇论文（ICLR、NeurIPS、EMNLP）构建，约 40K 条实例；对齐精度 0.95，召回率 0.93，F1 0.94，κ 0.85。

experiments.title: 基准评估
experiments.detail: ActReview‑Bench 包含 1,000 条人工筛选实例；模型在诊断质量、修订质量、弱点有效性、技术正确性、解决充分性和审稿人有用性上进行评估。

experiments.title: 人工评估
experiments.detail: 在 175 条留出实例上，ActReview‑RL 的调整后胜率 >50% 超过先前的专用模型；修订有用性的平均评分高于基线，而技术准确性仍低于人工评审。

findings.title: 可操作性与依据性提升
findings.detail: ActReview 在可操作性和依据性指标上优于先前的专用评审生成模型，同时匹配强大的提示式 LLM。

findings.title: 修订有用性提升
findings.detail: 人工评审在审稿人有用性维度上给 ActReview 的修订建议打分高于基线。

findings.title: 技术准确性差距
findings.detail: 尽管有用性提升，生成的修订在技术正确性上仍低于人工撰写的反馈。

findings.title: 泛化性与鲁棒性
findings.detail: 分析表明在留出论文和独立评审之间表现一致（Cohen’s κ 0.71）。

contributions: Rebuttal‑guided dataset (ActReview‑40K) linking reviewer weaknesses to author actions
Dual‑task formulation 将诊断与可操作建议分离
Weakness‑specific rubric rewards 用于强化学习 (GRPO)
ActReview‑Bench benchmark 用于评估诊断和修订质量

方法依赖 author rebuttals 的可用性，限制了其在没有公开 rebuttal 线程的会议上的适用性
评估基于有限的人类评分样本；指标的可扩展性尚未证明

rubric‑based RL 能否高效扩展到更大的 LLM 或缺乏 rebuttal 数据的领域？
数据选择粒度（例如 atomic weaknesses）与模型性能之间的权衡是什么？

papers.title: Tracing the Roots: A Multi-Agent Framework for Uncovering Data Lineage in Post-Training LLMs
papers.abstract: Post-training data plays a pivotal role in shaping the capabilities of Large Language Models (LLMs), yet datasets are often treated as isolated artifacts, overlooking the systemic connections that underlie their evolution. To disentangle these complex relationships, we introduce the concept of \textbf{data lineage} to the LLM ecosystem and propose an automated multi-agent framework to reconstruct the evolutionary graph of dataset development. Through large-scale lineage analysis, we characterize domain-specific structural patterns, such as vertical refinement in Math-oriented datasets and horizontal aggregation in General-domain corpora. Moreover, we uncover pervasive systemic issues, including \textit{structural redundancy} induced by implicit dataset intersections and the \textit{propagation of benchmark contamination} along lineage paths. To demonstrate the practical value of lineage analysis for data construction, we leverage the reconstructed lineage graph to create a \textit{lineage-aware diversity-oriented dataset}. By anchoring instruction sampling at upstream leaf sources, this approach mitigates downstream homogenization and hidden redundancy, yielding a more diverse post-training corpus. We further highlight lineage-centric analysis as an efficient and robust topological alternative to sample-level dataset comparison for large-scale data ecosystems. By grounding data construction in explicit lineage structures, our work advances post-training data curation toward a more systematic and controllable paradigm.

papers.title: Mechanistic Data Attribution: Tracing the Training Origins of Interpretable LLM Units
papers.abstract: While mechanistic interpretability has identified interpretable circuits in large language models (LLMs), their causal origins in training data remain elusive. We introduce *mechanistic data attribution* (MDA), a scalable framework that employs influence functions to trace interpretable units back to specific training samples. Through extensive experiments on the Pythia family, we causally validate that targeted intervention—removing or augmenting a small fraction of high-influence samples—significantly modulates the emergence of interpretable heads, whereas random interventions show no effect. Our analysis reveals that repetitive structural data (e.g., LaTeX, XML) acts as a mechanistic catalyst. Furthermore, we observe that interventions targeting induction head formation induce a concurrent change in the model’s in-context learning (ICL) capability. This provides direct causal evidence for the long-standing hypothesis regarding the functional link between induction heads and ICL. Finally, we propose a mechanistic data augmentation pipeline that consistently accelerates circuit convergence across model scales, providing a principled methodology for steering the developmental trajectories of LLMs.

papers.title: How Learning Rate Decay Wastes Your Best Data in Curriculum-Based LLM Pretraining
papers.abstract: Due to the scarcity of high-quality data, large language models (LLMs) are often trained on mixtures of data with varying quality levels, even after sophisticated data curation. A natural approach to better leverage high-quality data is curriculum-based pretraining, where the model is trained on data sorted in ascending order of quality as determined by a quality metric. However, prior studies have reported limited improvements from such curriculum-based pretraining strategies. This work identifies a critical factor constraining these methods: the incompatibility between the ascending data quality order and the decaying learning rate (LR) schedule. We find that while curriculum-based training substantially outperforms random shuffling when using a constant LR, its advantage diminishes under standard LR decay schedules. Our experiments show this incompatibility can be mitigated by two simple strategies: (1) employing a more moderate LR decay schedule, where the final LR is only moderately smaller than the peak LR, and (2) replacing LR decay with model averaging, i.e., computing a weighted average of the final few checkpoints. By combining these strategies, we improve the average score on a suite of standard benchmarks by 1.64% over random shuffling, without additional data refinement. Validated on 1.5B-parameter models trained over 30B tokens with various data-quality metrics, our findings call for a re-evaluation of curriculum-based LLM pretraining and underscore the potential of co-designing data curricula with optimization methods.

papers.title: Don't Drop Dropout: Optimizing Layer Sparsity for Efficient LLM Training and Inference
papers.abstract: Layer dropout (a.k.a. stochastic depth) has been shown to enable faster training, higher accuracy, and robustness to zero-shot layer pruning in both language and vision transformers. However, as models and datasets have scaled, dropout - particularly layer dropout - has largely disappeared from large language models (LLMs) pre-training recipes. While some prior work has reported that dropout can degrade accuracy, no comprehensive study has quantified, let alone mitigated, this effect. In this study, we show that layer dropout should be used in state-of-the-art LLM training, establishing best practices and scaling analysis for both training and post-training benefits. Concretely, with optimal layer distribution, time schedule, and optimizer hyperparameters, we observe that at the same training FLOPs layer dropout leads to lower loss. For a given number of training steps, LLMs can achieve lower or similar validation loss while saving upto 25% of training FLOPs. Moreover, layer dropout enables significant post-training optimizations, such as early exit, intermediate-layer skipping, and self-speculative decoding, yielding up to 1.5x inference speedup with negligible accuracy loss. Across more than 2400 training experiments, spanning models from 271M to 8.2B parameters and datasets up to 160B tokens, we demonstrate that these findings extend reliably to large-scale training regimes. All pre-training experiments were run on Cerebras CS-3 systems.

papers.title: PRICE: A Systematic Study of LLM Adaptation Choices for Bitcoin Price Forecasting
papers.abstract: Cryptocurrency markets exhibit extreme volatility and non-stationary dynamics that challenge conventional forecasting methods. Although Large Language Models (LLMs) have shown promise for time series forecasting, the combined effects of adaptation choices remain largely unexplored in financial settings. This study introduces PRICE, a structured approach for adapting LLMs to short-term Bitcoin price forecasting. Built on a 4-bit quantized LLaMA-3 8B model, PRICE investigates how fine-tuning, numerical representation, prompting, inference, and decoding jointly influence forecasting performance. PRICE integrates Parameter-efficient fine-tuning with Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA), Recursive multi-step inference, Integer-rounded numerical representation, Context-Task-Format (CTF) prompting, and Exact zero-temperature decoding. Ablation studies show that each component contributes to forecasting accuracy and reliability. LoRA enables efficient training on limited hardware, recursive inference improves accuracy, integer-rounded values reduce errors, CTF prompting outperforms Chain-of-Thought, Implicit Chain-of-Thought (iCoT), and few-shot prompting, and zero-temperature decoding improves stability during recursive forecasting. Comparative evaluation against eight transformer-based and time-series foundation models shows that PRICE achieves the lowest forecasting errors on both validation and test sets while maintaining robust performance across evaluation periods. Despite being based on a model primarily pretrained on text rather than time-series data, PRICE achieves competitive or superior performance relative to specialized foundation models. These findings demonstrate that adaptation choices critically determine the accuracy and robustness of LLMs for numerical time-series forecasting.

summary.takeaway: PRICE 表明，系统组合 LoRA 微调、递归推理、整数四舍五入输入、CTF 提示和零温度解码，可在所有评估基线中实现最低的比特币价格预测误差。

deep_dive.overview: 本文提出 PRICE 框架，系统地将 4‑bit 量化 LLaMA‑3 8B 模型适配用于短期比特币价格预测。它将 LoRA 参数高效微调、递归多步推理、整数四舍五入价格表示、Context‑Task‑Format 提示和精确零温度解码五个正交适配选择整合为一条流水线。通过受控消融分析评估各选择的影响，并在与八个 transformer 与 time‑series 基础模型的广泛基准测试中评估整体性能。结果表明，各组件均带来可测量的提升，完整系统在验证集和测试集上均实现最低预测误差。

papers.title: Distill Globally, Adapt Locally: Reasoning Distillation and Product-Type Test-Time Training for Scalable Trade-Up Recommendation
papers.abstract: Trade-up recommendation identifies higher-quality alternatives that preserve a customer's purchase intent while offering upgraded benefits. Large language models (LLMs) can reason about such distinctions, but applying them directly to hundreds of millions of product pairs is operationally impractical. We introduce a two-level framework that distills LLM reasoning into an efficient non-generative student and adapts its decision boundary to product-type-specific trade-up criteria. At Level 1, a retrieval-augmented few-shot LLM teacher generates structured relation labels and natural-language rationales. These rationales supervise a compact embedding-pair classifier through alignment and contrastive objectives; at inference, the student uses only two precomputed 768-dimensional product embeddings, with no LLM calls or text generation. On a fixed human-annotated benchmark of 8,352 pairs, a 15.5M-parameter four-class reasoning-distilled student achieves AUC 0.924 (95% CI [0.918, 0.929]), compared with 0.912 for the four-class label-only student. At Level 2, product-type test-time training (PT-TTT) uses few-shot demonstrations to optimize lightweight category-specific adapters over the frozen student. PT-TTT improves AUC from 0.924 to 0.941 and average precision from 0.920 to 0.940. On a 100K-pair proxy catalog, the distilled student on a single eight-GPU machine is approximately 5,000x faster and 10,000x lower in estimated cost than direct LLM inference.

papers.title: PLUME: Parameter-Efficient Personalization of Large Language Models via Low-Rank User Modulation in Shared Subspaces
papers.abstract: Personalizing large language models (LLMs) is essential for delivering AI assistance that aligns with individual users' styles, intents, and preferences. While per-user fine-tuning can substantially enhance personalization quality, it introduces significant parameter and storage overhead, limiting scalability to large user populations. We propose PLUME (Personalized Low-Rank Adaptation through User Modulation and Shared Subspace), a lightweight framework that achieves efficient and expressive per-user adaptation by leveraging a shared task-specific subspace. Specifically, PLUME first learns a global task subspace from aggregated user data. Personalization is then achieved by training only a lightweight small square matrix within this subspace, enabling each user to obtain a tailored model while keeping shared components fixed. Cross-layer shared parameters and rank-1 residual terms are further introduced to significantly reduce redundancy while maintaining expressiveness. Experiments on multiple personalized text generation benchmarks demonstrate that PLUME achieves comparable or superior performance to strong baselines, while reducing per-user parameters by over 95%. These results establish shared-subspace modulation with minimal residuals as a scalable and semantically grounded approach to LLM personalization.

summary.takeaway: PLUME 实现了超过 95% 的每用户参数削减，同时在个性化文本生成上匹配或超越强基线。

papers.title: A Removal Based Approach to Improve LLM Faithfulness at Test-Time
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used for consequential decisions, making their explanations an important tool for auditing model behavior. Unfortunately, these explanations can be unfaithful, failing to reflect the actual reasoning underlying the model's decisions. We consider a setting in which an LLM provides both an answer and an explanation in response to a question. We identify two distinct dimensions of unfaithful explanations: incompleteness, meaning that the explanation omits factors that influence the answer, and unsoundness, meaning that the explanation cites factors that did not influence the model's answer. Existing approaches to improving LLM faithfulness include training-time methods, which require access to model weights and extensive computational resources, and test-time methods that largely focus on addressing unsoundness. We introduce a test-time approach that directly targets incompleteness. We remove from the input the concepts not credited in the model's explanation and re-query the model on the reduced input. This eliminates unmentioned influences while preserving the influence of mentioned concepts. Across two datasets, multiple model families, and two independent faithfulness metrics, our approach improves explanation faithfulness compared to both standard prompting and prompting to encourage faithfulness. Our method is model-agnostic and can be applied at inference time without modifying model parameters, providing a flexible mechanism for reducing hidden influences and improving the reliability and safety of LLM-assisted decision making.

papers.title: LLM-Assisted Behavioural and Scenario Augmentation for Agent-Based Energy Adoption Models
papers.abstract: Recent advances in large language models (LLMs) create opportunities to enrich simulation-based energy policy analysis, particularly by supporting structured behavioural assumptions and exploratory techno-economic scenarios. However, directly replacing adoption models with LLM reasoning raises concerns regarding interpretability, reproducibility, and behavioural validity. This paper proposes a hybrid framework for LLM-assisted specification design, integrating bounded behavioural rubrics and structured scenario specifications into a calibrated agent-based model (ABM) of solar photovoltaic (PV) adoption by Irish dairy farms. The proposed approach preserves the original techno-economic adoption mechanism while augmenting it with bounded behavioural modulation and scenario-driven uncertainty analysis. Behavioural effects are represented through interpretable conservative, balanced, and optimistic rubrics, while future policy and market conditions are explored through fixed, rule-validated scenario specifications. Experimental results across multiple policy settings, Monte Carlo worlds, and random seeds demonstrate stable and economically plausible behaviour, with adoption outcomes remaining bounded and monotonic across behavioural regimes. The framework achieves up to approximately 13% behavioural adoption increase relative to the corresponding logistic case without producing unstable or unrealistic saturation dynamics. The results demonstrate that LLM-assisted specifications can be integrated into calibrated energy ABMs in a controlled, reproducible, and policy-relevant manner.

summary.takeaway: LLM 辅助的行为和情景规范可增强已校准的 ABM，实现适度的采纳提升且保持稳定。

papers.title: STAIR (STructure Aware Information Retriever): A novel dataset and LLM based retriever for document structure augmentation
papers.abstract: Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) is a key component for generating accurate and hallucination free answers using Large Language Models (LLMs). LLMs are improving at handling long context, but still suffer from "lost in the middle" problem. Thus, precise and accurate retrieval is important. Current retrievers chunk long context into length-based manageable chunks - in the process throwing away rich and informative semantic global structure in the corpus. We introduce a novel retrieval system STAIR that empowers an LLM to exploit global structure in a corpus such as a Table of Contents (ToC) to efficiently store and retrieve information from its model parameters. Our thorough and careful ablation studies with a finetuned Differentiable Search Index (DSI) system show that ToC helps build a low hallucination (less than 0.05%) generative Information Retrieval (IR) system and can generalize to examples where very few training samples are available. To further research in this novel direction of ToC based retrieval we release SearchTome - a diverse benchmark created from 18 books across 6 diverse domains to further research in this novel direction. STAIR achieves a high Recall@1 score of 82.6% on SearchTome as compared to DSI (76.9%), where the difference is found to be statistically significant. STAIR easily beats other strong baselines such as BM25 (59.5%), DPR (68.7%) and out-of-the-box Mistral (13.8%).

summary.takeaway: Incorporating Table of Contents structure into a model‑based retriever yields substantially higher Recall@1 and near‑zero hallucinations.
summary.problem: Chunk‑based retrievers discard global semantic structure, leading to imprecise retrieval and hallucinations in Retrieval‑Augmented Generation.
summary.method: STAIR fine‑tunes a Differentiable Search Index (DSI) LLM with ToC inputs, enabling direct generation of leaf‑node identifiers.
summary.evidence: STAIR attains 82.6% Recall@1 on SearchTome, a 7.4‑point gain over vanilla DSI, while hallucination rate stays below 0.05%.
summary.limitations: Evaluation is confined to corpora that already provide a Table of Contents, limiting generality to unstructured data.
summary.why_for_you: The work directly addresses trustworthy LLM generation by reducing hallucinations through structural cues, relevant to your interests in reliable LLM behavior.

signals.text: STAIR introduces a ToC‑aware retrieval system achieving 82.6% Recall@1 on the new SearchTome benchmark.
It fine‑tunes a DSI model with hierarchical ToC inputs, letting the LLM generate leaf‑node IDs without memorizing structure.
Recall@1 improves 7.4 points over vanilla DSI and hallucinations stay <0.05%, but only on corpora with existing ToC.

deep_dive.overview: STAIR tackles the "lost in the middle" issue of long‑context LLMs by exploiting the inherent hierarchical organization of documents via their Table of Contents. The authors construct a hierarchical tree from the ToC, embed and cluster sections, and fine‑tune a Differentiable Search Index (DSI) model using LoRA adapters. Experiments on the newly released SearchTome benchmark (18 books, 6 domains) show that ToC‑augmented retrieval markedly outperforms traditional baselines (BM25, DPR) and a vanilla DSI, while dramatically lowering hallucination rates. Limitations stem from the reliance on pre‑existing structural metadata.

methodology.title: Model fine‑tuning
methodology.detail: Mistral Instruct v0.2 is fine‑tuned for up to 200 epochs with LoRA (r=16, α=32), early‑stopping on dev Recall@1, using a 14k token input window for STAIR and 512 tokens for DSI.

methodology.title: Hierarchical tree construction
methodology.detail: Documents are recursively embedded, clustered, and summarized to form a tree mirroring the Table of Contents, providing structured prompts to the model.

mechanism.title: Model‑based indexing with ToC
mechanism.detail: The LLM stores the entire corpus in its parameters and, given a query plus ToC context, directly generates the identifier of the leaf node containing the answer, bypassing the need to memorize individual sections.

mechanism.title: Hallucination mitigation
mechanism.detail: By constraining outputs to valid leaf identifiers, the system reduces generation of non‑leaf (invalid) nodes, achieving a hallucination rate near zero regardless of training sample size.

experiments.title: Benchmarks and baselines
experiments.detail: SearchTome benchmark (18 books, 6 domains) evaluated with Recall@1, Recall@3, nDCG@3 via BeIR; baselines include BM25, DPR (NV‑Embed‑v2), out‑of‑the‑box Mistral, and a fine‑tuned vanilla DSI.

experiments.title: Results
experiments.detail: STAIR: R@1 82.6%; DSI: 76.9%; BM25: 59.5%; DPR: 68.7%; Mistral: 13.8%; hallucination <0.05%; statistical significance reported for the R@1 gap.

findings.title: ToC improves retrieval accuracy
findings.detail: Incorporating ToC yields a 7.4% absolute increase in Recall@1 over DSI, especially for leaf nodes with few training examples.

findings.title: Reduced hallucinations
findings.detail: STAIR maintains a near‑zero hallucination rate across training regimes, unlike DSI which shows higher rates for low‑frequency leaf nodes.

contributions: ToC‑aware retrieval system (STAIR) that leverages model‑based indexing.
SearchTome benchmark providing structured ToC data for long‑context retrieval.
Empirical demonstration of hallucination reduction via structural constraints.
limitations: Current evaluation limited to corpora with existing global structure (Table of Contents).
No experiments on standard unstructured retrieval benchmarks.
open_questions: How does ToC‑augmented retrieval perform on documents lacking explicit hierarchical metadata?
Can structural prompting be combined with adversarial training to further improve robustness?
What effects does ToC integration have on the loss landscape and parameter dynamics of the underlying LLM?

papers.title: Representational alignment yields generalizable safety in language models
papers.abstract: Aligning large language models (LLMs) is essential for their safe deployment. Current alignment methods mainly optimize observable responses, yet models remain vulnerable when the same harmful intent is recast in unfamiliar or adversarial forms that humans can easily recognize. Prototype theory offers an account of this adaptability. Human concepts are represented around central cases, and new instances are categorized according to their graded typicality relative to these prototypes. Here we show that such categorization of moral concepts is weakly preserved in current LLMs. Across 23 LLMs, models often failed to distinguish opposed moral categories or preserve fine-grained typicality within each category. These deficits persist across parameter sizes and alignment stages. We developed representational similarity optimization, which directly aligns the latent representations in LLMs with the categorization expressed in human moral judgements, without supervising generated responses. In matched experiments using the same 251,334 moral annotations, standard behavioral alignment learned the intended moral judgements at the response level while leaving the categorization structure largely unchanged and increasing vulnerability across adversarial evaluations. Reorganizing moral categorization produced more modest gains in explicit judgements but consistently improved adversarial robustness across model scales on diverse benchmarks and attack strategies. Our findings provide functional support for the view that prototype-based categorization contributes to behavioral adaptability. They also show that transferring this representational principle to LLMs yields generalizable safety under adversarial conditions.

summary.evidence: 在251,334个道德标注的实验中，标准行为对齐仅提升响应层面道德判断，而表示对齐显著提高对抗鲁棒性。
summary.limitations: 未提及具体限制，但指出需进一步验证跨不同任务的泛化性。
summary.method: 开发表示相似性优化，直接对齐LLM潜在表示与人类道德判断分类，无需监督生成响应。
summary.problem: 当前对齐方法无法有效应对有害意图的重新表述，导致模型在对抗性评估中易受攻击。
summary.takeaway: 通过表示相似性优化直接对齐LLM的潜在表示与人类道德判断，提升对抗性条件下的通用安全性。
summary.why_for_you: 提升对抗性鲁棒性，符合高效对抗训练需求。

papers.title: ALRA: Adaptive Local Relational Alignment for Logit-Based Pre-training Distillation of Autoregressive Language Models
papers.abstract: Logit-based knowledge distillation for autoregressive language models usually aligns teacher and student next-token distributions over the entire vocabulary. However, this global objective overlooks relative preferences among likely token alternatives. Existing local approaches often select candidate tokens from either the teacher or the student alone. Teacher-only selection can miss tokens that the student considers likely, while student-only selection can rely on an inaccurate ranking early in training. We propose Adaptive Local Relational Alignment (ALRA), a position-specific framework combining student proposals with teacher guidance. At each valid prediction position, the student proposes likely tokens, while the teacher's most probable token is included as an anchor. ALRA adjusts the number of selected tokens according to how broadly the teacher distributes probability within this candidate set relative to the current batch. Adaptive Local Divergence retains the mass-matching term and separately matches the relative token distributions within the selected and remaining vocabulary regions. Unlike the exact full-vocabulary decomposition, it replaces the teacher-mass coefficients of the two conditional terms with unit coefficients, preventing either term from being downweighted solely because its region has low teacher probability. Student-Weighted Pairwise Relational Alignment emphasizes high-probability token pairs with small student probability gaps and gives less weight to unlikely or clearly separated pairs. Experiments on The Pile with randomly initialized 200M- and 500M-parameter students across nine zero-shot benchmarks yield average accuracies of 36.62% and 37.40%. ALRA exceeds the strongest competing distillation baseline by 0.94 and 0.83 percentage points and improves over pre-training without distillation by 2.31 and 2.91 points, respectively.

summary.problem: 全局 KL 蒸馏忽略了 token 相对偏好，现有局部方法仅依赖教师或学生的 token 排名。
summary.why_for_you: 符合您对 on‑policy 蒸馏的兴趣，提供了一种用于预训练的全新自适应蒸馏目标。
summary.takeaway: ALRA 的自适应局部 token 选择为自回归语言模型带来了最先进的蒸馏提升。
summary.method: ALRA 从学生的 top token 构建位置特定候选集，并加入教师 top‑1 锚点，自适应调整其规模，随后使用 Adaptive Local Divergence 与 Student‑Weighted Pairwise Relational Alignment 损失。
summary.limitations: 在可得来源中未说明。
summary.evidence: 在 The Pile 上的实验中，200M 与 500M 学生模型分别达到 36.62% 与 37.40% 的平均 zero‑shot 准确率，超出最强基线 0.94 与 0.83 个百分点。

mechanism.title: Dynamic Candidate Budget
mechanism.detail: 该算法计算教师概率分布的批次级统计量，并调整每个位置的 token 预算 (d_min, d_max)，在教师分布更平坦的区域分配更多 token。

mechanism.title: Unit Coefficient Mass Decoupling
mechanism.detail: 在条件 KL 项中将教师质量系数替换为 1，ALRA 确保选中区域和其余区域无论教师概率质量大小都同等贡献。

experiments.title: Pre‑training Distillation on The Pile
experiments.detail: 教师固定为 Qwen1.5‑1.8B；学生为随机初始化的 Qwen‑200M 与 Qwen‑500M；约 1 B token 预算；九个 zero‑shot 基准；基线包括 Vanilla KD、PD、ATKD、RLD、LDRLD、TAD、BiLD。

signals.text: ALRA 引入自适应局部 token 选择，将学生提议与教师锚点结合，提升蒸馏性能。
Student‑Weighted Pairwise Relational Alignment 根据学生概率差距为高概率 token 对加权。
200M 与 500M 学生达到 36.62%/37.40% 的平均 zero‑shot 准确率，分别比最佳基线提升 +0.94/+0.83。

deep_dive.overview: ALRA 通过构建位置特定的 token 集，将学生提出的高概率 token 与教师的 top‑1 锚点合并，以解决全局 KL 蒸馏的低效问题。该方法根据教师概率分布的散度自适应确定集合规模，随后使用带单位系数的 Adaptive Local Divergence 保持质量匹配，并通过 Student‑Weighted Pairwise Relational Alignment 强调学生间隙较小的 token 对。在 The Pile 上使用 200M 与 500M Qwen 学生模型进行评估，ALRA 在九个 zero‑shot 基准上超越所有先前基于 logits 的 KD 基线。
contributions: 用于基于 logits 的预训练蒸馏的 Adaptive Local Relational Alignment 框架。

findings.title: Performance Gains
findings.detail: 200M 学生实现 36.62% 的平均准确率（比最佳基线提升 +0.94，较无 KD 提升 +2.31）；500M 学生实现 37.40% 的平均准确率（比最佳基线提升 +0.83，较无 KD 提升 +2.91）。

methodology.title: Adaptive Local Token Set Construction
methodology.detail: 在每个预测位置，学生提供其 top‑k 可能 token；教师的最高概率 token 作为锚点加入，并根据批次内教师概率离散度对选取 token 数量进行缩放。

methodology.title: Adaptive Local Divergence (ALD)
methodology.detail: 保留全局质量匹配项，同时在选中词表区域和其余区域分别匹配相对分布，使用单位系数避免对低概率区域降权。

methodology.title: Student‑Weighted Pairwise Relational Alignment (SWPRA)
methodology.detail: 计算 token 对的成对对齐损失，并依据学生的概率差距为每对加权，使高概率且排名接近的 token 对获得更强监督。

limitations: 在可得来源中未说明。
open_questions: ALRA 在更大学生模型或下游微调场景下的可扩展性如何？

papers.title: Gradients Know What Outcomes Don't: Unlocking Reinforcement Learning for LLM Reasoning with Gradient-Aligned Rewards
papers.abstract: Reinforcement learning from verifiable rewards (RLVR) drives chain-of-thought reasoning in large language models, yet its binary outcome reward cannot distinguish among correct trajectories. Existing dense reward alternatives, from surface heuristics to process reward models, either ignore the expert solutions already present in training corpora or require expensive offline annotation. We propose Gradient-Aligned Reward (GAR), which operates in the policy's own gradient space: truncated backpropagation through the output projection layer extracts a compact gradient vector for each rollout, and cosine similarity with an expert-anchor gradient yields a dense, reasoning-aware reward with less than 9% wall-clock overhead. We prove that this cosine admits a multiplicative decomposition into prediction-error and activation-pattern factors, providing a concrete characterization of what the alignment signal measures. On Qwen3-4B and Qwen3-8B, GAR consistently improves over GRPO and other baselines on competition-level math benchmarks and transfers to GPQA Diamond and MMLU-Pro without domain-specific data. Code and data are available at https://github.com/LQgdwind/GAR.

summary.evidence: GAR improves Qwen3-4B/8B over GRPO on math benchmarks and transfers to GPQA Diamond/MMLU-Pro with <9% wall-clock overhead.
summary.limitations: GAR has not been deployed in industrial production environments.
summary.method: GAR uses truncated backpropagation through the output projection layer to extract gradient vectors, scoring rollouts via cosine similarity with expert-anchor gradients.
summary.problem: Binary outcome rewards in RLVR cannot distinguish correct reasoning trajectories, leading to flat policy gradients.
summary.takeaway: Gradient-Aligned Reward (GAR) improves LLM reasoning via gradient-space cosine similarity with expert anchors, achieving <9% overhead and math benchmark gains.
summary.why_for_you: This paper directly addresses efficient adversarial training for LLM reasoning by leveraging gradient-space alignment, matching your interest in loss landscape optimization.

contributions: Gradient-space process rewards from expert anchors
Multiplicative decomposition of alignment signal into prediction-error and activation-pattern factors
Dense supervision without additional annotation
<9% overhead in standard RLVR training

experiments.title: Models and data

experiments.detail: GRPO, REINFORCE++, MASPO, Grad2Reward, G2RL
experiments.title: Baselines
